An estimation of the $B^0_s\rightarrow K^+K^-$ decay time for $B^0_s$ mesons has been made with the help of around 37 picobarns of LHCb data from 2010. This measure allows for constraints on theories beyond the Standard Model that may influence the $B^0_s$ system and was found to be 1.440 picoseconds by employing two methods with varying degrees of uncertainty, specifically 0.096 (statistical) ± 0.008 (systematic) ± 0.003 (model-based).

This research paper focuses on the numerical solution of a stochastic control problem governed by a parabolic equation with the control variable affecting the diffusion coefficient, particularly with the presence of rough inputs; it establishes the convergence of a specific numerical discretization method and provides an alternative solution using a stochastic simulation technique known as the Monte-Carlo method.

Our in-depth examination of extremely energetic cosmic rays detected at the Pierre Auger Observatory reveals significant patterns of large-scale anisotropy. At the higher end of our energy range, a specific anisotropy signal was initially reported - namely, a right ascension-based dipolar modulation. To further investigate, we divided the most energetic group into three segments, and discovered that this anisotropy becomes increasingly pronounced with rising energy levels above 4 EeV, exhibiting an energy-dependent pattern that adheres to a power law with an index of 0.79 ± 0.19. We also discovered that the orientation of these anisotropy patterns supports their extragalactic origins, across all energy levels examined. Furthermore, an investigation of the quadrupolar component of anisotropy revealed patterns that could be attributed to local, terrestrial effects rather than cosmic sources. We interpret our findings within the context of theoretical models proposing that very energetic cosmic rays originate from radio galaxies that are actively emitting particles.

The ATLAS detector at the LHC gathered p+Pb data with a centre of mass energy of 5.02 TeV and 25 nanobarns of integrated luminosity, enabling a comparison with interpolated pp measurements at 2.76 and 7 TeV. This study examines the nuclear modification factor for charged particles in forward rapidities, focusing on transverse momentum ranging from 0.7 to 21 GeV. Results reveal a dependence on nuclear modification factor according to centrality, with the most significant variation occurring in the most peripheral collisions. Additionally, an increase in the normalized differential second-order anisotropy coefficient is observed in peripheral collisions and further explores the underlying physics through the coefficient of hard particles.

Quantum mechanics can be explored on noncommutative spaces, characterized by specific commutation relations that define the structure constants of a Lie algebra. By transforming the coordinates into linear differential operators in a commuting momentum space, we can reformulate this issue into an ordinary quantum problem. These operators, representing the coordinates $\hat x_a$, have a form $-i\hat D_a = -iE_{ab}(p)\partial /\partial p_b$, where $E_{ab}$ can be expressed as an infinite series over the deformation parameter $\theta$. The deformed Hamiltonian $\hat H$ describes the motion on corresponding group manifolds with sizes proportional to $\theta^{-1}$, whose metrics also appear in certain infinite series of $\theta$. The matrices $E_{ab}$ can be represented in simple forms for certain algebras like $su(2)$ and $u(N)$. Additionally, our study has yielded new nonstandard metric formulas for all the spheres $S^n$, projective spaces $RP^n$, and $U(2)$.

In evaluating the potential of federated learning, we tested its performance in training deep learning models to analyze digitized tissue samples, specifically in a classification application involving the detection of tumor cells within whole-slide images. By simulating a FL environment with a large, diverse dataset of cancer images from various sources, we compared the results of training models using both a federated approach and a centralized approach. Our findings indicate that federated learning can produce models with similar accuracy to those trained with centralized data, while avoiding the need to collect extensive training datasets at a single location. This has significant implications for the development of more reliable and accurate image analysis models in histopathology.

In this study, a high-speed optical transmission system is demonstrated, achieving a data rate of 72Gbit/s using the on-off keying technique over a 10.7km submarine cable that lacks dispersion compensation.  Chromatic dispersion in this underwater cable causes four signal nulls, severely hindering system performance. To address this issue, a novel detection method called the optimized decision method was developed to counter the dispersive effects, thereby enhancing system reliability and reducing errors. By employing this detection method, the required received power to maintain a 10% error rate is reduced by approximately 4dB when compared to conventional methods. As a result, this system can operate with up to 12dB less powerful signal amplification, which in turn helps extend the lifespan of the amplifier and reduces the risk of its failure in critical applications.

Deep Learning models like Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs) hold great promise for handling time-series data. TCNs leverage a technique called time-dilated convolution that poses an optimization challenge which typically demands significant experimentation. We've developed a technique to automate the dilation optimization process by casting it as a weight-pruning operation along the time axis. Our method learns dilation factors concurrently with weights during training and achieves notable gains in model compactness and inference efficiency without compromising accuracy. It produces a range of highly optimal TCN variants from a single starting model, surpassing the performance of custom-designed networks in both efficiency and accuracy.
This paper proves that any finite-dimensional Zinbiel algebra over a given field possesses a specific characteristic - nilpotency, building on a previous discovery that these algebras are solvable.

This study provides first-time data on the fluctuations of a specific angle, known as $\Psi_n$, and magnitude, known as $v_n$, related to particle flow, which have been determined using a newly developed technique for four-particle correlations. Researchers used ALICE to collect these data in high-energy Pb-Pb collisions at the LHC. Fluctuations in both angle and magnitude are evident across different centralities and become more pronounced in more central collisions and in collisions where the momentum of the particles is higher than 2 GeV/c. These findings, which have been compared to theoretical models such as iEBE-VISHNU, MUSIC, and AMPT, shed new light on the complex and not well understood initial conditions of these collisions. Furthermore, they highlight unique sensitivities to two crucial factors: the viscosity of quark--gluon plasma and the characteristics of the collisions' initial state. Given that these fluctuations tend to increase with the momentum of the particles, there is a need for re-examining existing theoretical models to gain a deeper understanding of this phenomenon.

The unified correspondence theory leverages the algebraic and order theoretic underpinnings of Sahlqvist correspondence to offer versatile tools for correspondence and canonicity across diverse semantic frameworks and signatures. These tools, specifically tailored to logics whose semantics rely on normal lattice expansions (DLEs), enable computation of first-order correspondents for inductive formulas using the algorithm ALBA. Conversely, our contribution introduces an inverse algorithm that utilizes ALBA's rules and parameters to derive the original inductive formula from its first-order correspondent in normal DLEs.

This research focuses on addressing inconsistencies in data tables that contain missing values and functional relationships. Unlike conventional approaches that require adherence to these dependencies, our work aims to explore theories for handling instances that breach certain dependencies, with no preconditions on the presence of missing values. We establish a framework where each data entry can be associated with a truth status: true, false, inconsistent, or undetermined. Furthermore, our framework facilitates examination of pressing problems like data quality assessments, query validation, and data merging. Specifically, we investigate query validation as the central problem of this research, building on the foundation established by recent studies. Key contributions of this research are (a) an innovative strategy for handling inconsistencies, (b) methods for determining the veracity of data tuples, and (c) an examination of our approach's relevance to Four-valued logic and answer set programming. Additionally, we provide an original solution to query validation and contrast it with existing works, ultimately outlining future directions for our research.

This study presents a novel dynamic econometric model called Time-Varying Poisson AutoRegressive with external covariates, specifically designed to analyze and forecast count-based time series data. Our research indicates that a score-driven approach is particularly effective in capturing the evolution of time-varying parameters and allows for modeling complex dynamics and shifts within such data sets. Furthermore, we have analyzed the theoretical characteristics of the TV-PARX model, demonstrating under mild conditions that maximum likelihood estimation yields reliable and normally-distributed estimates of model parameters. To evaluate the TV-PARX model's performance and forecasting capabilities in real-world scenarios, we conducted a series of Monte Carlo simulations. Additionally, we have applied the time-varying specification of the TV-PARX model to empirical data sets, analyzing new daily COVID-19 cases in Italy and corporate defaults in the US.

We introduce Neural Descriptor Fields (NDFs), a novel object representation that
replicates both object points and relative poses in relation to a target, using
category-level descriptors. We apply this representation in object manipulation,
with the aim of repeating tasks on new object instances from the same category
after witnessing a single demonstration. To achieve this, we use optimization
to locate the pose whose descriptor corresponds to that in the demonstration. NDFs
are efficiently trained without expert input, using a self-supervised 3D
auto-encoder, and exhibit robust performance across 6-DoF rotations and translations.
In experiments, NDFs master tasks from just a handful (5-10) demonstrations,
in both simulation and with a physical robot. Results show our method excels at
generalizing over different object instances and poses, surpassing a comparison
method relying on 2D descriptors. The NDF project is hosted at https://yilundu.github.io/ndf/.

The SiD Detector is one of the two validated detector designs for the future ILC, specifically tailored to meet precision demands for the Higgs boson and other research areas while maintaining an adaptable sensitivity to diverse potential discoveries. The SiD's robust silicon vertex and tracking system, complemented by its high central magnetic field, ensures precise momentum measurement. The detector's finely granulated calorimeter system, designed for particle flow analysis, delivers accurate energy resolution across a wide energy range. Given the approaching construction timeline for the ILC, the time has come to reassess the design choices made during the design phase and incorporate the recent breakthroughs in technology into the review process. This review will discuss R&D prospects and participation opportunities for the SiD's development areas.

We performed the first in-depth analysis of seven red giant members in the globular cluster Tononzintla 2. We used the APOGEE-2 near-infrared spectra to examine the abundance levels of multiple chemical species in these stars. The findings showed a moderate metal content and the absence of an internal variation in metal abundance. Tononzintla 2 displayed an increased presence of alpha-enrichment which aligns with patterns observed in other rich-metallic galactic clusters. A nitrogen spread was discovered in Tononzintla 2 with multiple nitrogen-rich stars residing within it, significantly above average levels for this region, suggesting a multi-generational population within the cluster that consists of first-generation nitrogen-abundance members. A [Ce/Fe] spread was also detected, however the underlying relation between these elements and metal content remains unclear. Based on the characteristics shared with the cluster 2MASS-GGC-0353+00, Tononzintla 2 is suspected to reside at a distance of roughly 26.5 kpc from the galactic center. By constructing a field star comparison sample based on iron content and alpha-enrichment patterns, we inferred Tononzintla 2's formation timeline to be in line with the early formation period of the galaxy, specifically during its first ten billion years.

The Isabelle Archive of Formal Proofs has amassed substantial size over recent years, representing an impressive compilation of research and offering a diverse range of opportunities for statistical exploration in the field of theorem proving. Despite the numerous contributions made so far, the ever-expanding nature of the archive still poses certain challenges: locating specific content has become increasingly difficult, making it essential to prioritize reuse and clarity of comprehension. This thesis proposal outlines my research objectives, which focus on these concerns, as well as initial findings, which reveal that the Isabelle Archive exhibits characteristics typical of scale-free networks, as evidenced by the distribution of node in-degrees in its dependency graph.

Using the functional renormalization group at the next-to-leading order in the derivative expansion, we have updated the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for O(N) universality classes in classic scenarios. Specifically for QCD's relevant universality classes in three dimensions, we have determined the position of the Yang-Lee edge singularity for any N greater than or equal to 2, and for N equal to 2 we find |z_c|/R_chi^{1/gamma} equals 2.167(5), 1.542(11), and 1.432(11) for the corresponding degeneracy rates of 1, 2, and 3. Additionally, we have investigated the impact of the functional renormalization group's choice of optimal momentum parameter on the critical behavior at the Yang-Lee edge singularity, and found that using the optimal parameter has minimal impact less than proportions of 10^-3.

In statistics and machine learning, it is frequently essential to establish whether a basic optimization method on a non-convex function can eventually enter a region where the function becomes locally convex. To address this, we developed an inequality that enables us to analyze the properties of the optimization landscape surrounding the solutions produced by an approximate message passing (AMP) algorithm. Specifically, we applied our inequality to demonstrate the local convexity of a particular TAP free energy function, which is relevant to the Z2 synchronization problem and the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model. Additionally, our inequality led to a confirmation of a previous conjecture regarding the efficiency of a sampling algorithm in the "easy" regime of these models.

Modern metasurfaces, at the intersection of advanced technology and science,  
constitute an intricate field, involving electromagnetic systems characterized by  
thin, expansive, and minutely featured particles that can also vary spatially,  
temporally, and linearly.  To tackle this intricacy, researchers need to employ a  
unified approach, integrating theoretical design and analysis methods, supported  
by an established framework.  Recent breakthroughs, facilitated by Generalized  
Sheet Transition Conditions in combination with surface susceptibilities,  
now enable designers to develop intricate metasurfaces, addressing longstanding  
challenges.  This paper delves into computational modeling of these complex  
structures through GSTC-susceptibility methodology and underscores its critical  
importance in the holistic design of metasurfaces, reviewing the evolution of  
recent frequency and time-domain computational methods.

The primary objective of this research is to validate the smooth local orbital linearization theorem for smooth vector fields with a full set of nearby first integrals, especially those at nondegenerate singular points. This theoretical validation relies heavily on key concepts, including the formal orbital linearization theorem for formally integrable vector fields, the application of the blowing-up technique, and the application of the Sternberg-Chen theorem regarding formally equivalent smooth hyperbolic vector fields.

This report outlines the development of an Electron Correlation Potential Neural Network (eCPNN) that can determine effective potential functions for many-electron atoms through a data-driven approach, facilitated by Artificial Neural Networks. Trained in a fully inclusive manner with Single-Determinant Wavefunctions, this network successfully replicates a wide range of fundamental properties of these atoms. Our primary objective is to demonstrate the capability of eCPNN in pinpointing Highly Excited States that are challenging to identify using conventional self-consistent field methods. Our results show that in many-electron atoms, the trained eCPNN can pinpoint multiple valence electron states within various shell configurations and locate several Rydberg states that were previously unknown. Our findings also reveal that the electron density distributions and one-electron transition probabilities obtained from eCPNN comparisons to exact configurations yield precise results. Notably, our findings indicate that the trained potential can pinpoint several Highly Excited States, including multiple valence electron states and several Rydberg states that were previously unknown.

We have serendipitously identified a massive arc-like structure, dubbed a Giant Arc, which lies at a redshift of 0.8. Spanning nearly 1 billion light-years, this feature exhibits remarkable symmetry when viewed from space. It was discovered through a novel approach using intervening magnesium-absorbing systems in the light from background quasars. Our analysis leverages a range of techniques: hierarchical clustering, a statistical test, and power spectrum analysis - each method providing unique insights, which together suggest the presence of a massive structure at around 4.5 to 4.8 sigma confidence levels. We estimate that the arc-like feature contains a massive structure with a total mass of approximately $10^{20}$ times that of our sun, with an oval shape and a slight tilt. It's worth noting that such a large and complex structure like the Giant Arc challenges the cosmological principle under debate. It could be an isolated anomaly or a harbinger of more massive arc-like structures yet to be discovered.

While using photometry from stars to monitor the atmosphere may seem uncomplicated for optical astrophysics, achieving a precision of 0.01 for measuring the aerosol depth has been challenging. By taking wide-field photometry over a broad altitude range, the aerosol depth can be determined quickly, regardless of the system's absolute calibration, and even provides calibration as a by-product. Our team used extensive data from the FRAM telescope at the Pierre Auger Observatory and a custom-built telescope at the Chacra Observatory to improve the precision of this technique to a precision of possibly 0.01. To do this, we gathered over 140 days of data at the Pierre Auger Observatory in 2017 and 2018 to determine the aerosol depth in real-time for all optical observations published by the Collaborative International Real-time Observatory Network in 2019. These observations were collected using 12 wide-field telescopes at seven locations in Latin America. The resulting data showed an average aerosol depth of 0.12 with a standard deviation of 0.075. The technique was further refined to also account for calibration issues, resulting in a precision of possibly 0.01.

Recently, estimating a 6D object pose using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) has gained significant interest. Literature can be broadly categorized into two main areas based on whether intermediate cues are employed: direct methods and two-stage pipelines. In the latter category, CNN regresses intermediate cues such as object coordinates or virtual control points instead of pose parameters in the initial stage. Object pose is then resolved through the construction of correspondence constraints utilizing these intermediate cues. This study concentrates on refining two-stage pipelines by combining two distinct concepts: projection grouping on one hand and correspondence learning on the other. We initially employ a patch-based method to forecast projection heatmaps, representing the likelihood distribution of projected corners from 3D bounding boxes. Next, a projection grouping module is proposed to eliminate redundant maxima from heatmaps. Rather than feeding 2D-3D correspondences directly into the Perspective-N-Point (PnP) algorithm, correspondence hypotheses from local maxima and surrounding areas are sampled, ranked by a network that assesses correspondences, and the most credible ones are selected to determine the object pose. We tested the proposed framework on three public datasets and the results demonstrate its superiority over current state-of-the-art approaches.

Peridynamic theories have seen a significant expansion in their application across multiple disciplines, due to their ability to model and track discontinuity formation within materials. Bond-based Peridynamics, despite its modeling restrictions, has become a widely-used approach in numerical simulations because of its ease of implementation and intuitive connection to real-world physics. This paper delves into the aspects of bond-based peridynamic models, providing a thorough examination of the theory and its numerical representations. Various bond-based PD integral kernels have been presented along with their distinguishing characteristics, leading to discussions on their implications and common traits. A closer examination was conducted on the role of non-locality in determining motion, the interplay between kernel structure and material non-penetration, as well as the influence of PD kernel non-linearity on predicting fracture development. Finally, an exploration is initiated on adapting BB-PD to model fluids within the context of fading memory materials, suggesting directions for enhanced understanding of fluid dynamics through peridynamics.

We present GGLasso, a Python library designed to address General Graphical Lasso
challenges. Based on the original work of Friedman (2007), Graphical Lasso
estimates a sparsely constructed inverse covariance matrix $\Theta$ from
multivariate Gaussian data $\mathcal{X}$, initially introduced by Dempster (1972)
under Covariance Selection. The framework has been expanded to accommodate
hidden variables in Chandrasekaran (2012) and can jointly estimate multiple
inverse covariance matrices, as shown in Danaher (2013) and Tomasi (2018). The
GGLasso package supports the resolution of diverse formulations and notable
subcases like Graphical Lasso with latent variables, Group, and Fused Graphical Lasso.

Numerous numerical methods for resolving stochastic differential equations in molecular dynamics simulations have been scrutinized and assessed, focusing on deterministic impulses, drifts, and Brownian motions. By utilizing the Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff expansion, recent studies found that the methods' accuracy could be evaluated in terms of the impact of the step size on configurational averaging. Results showed that for harmonic oscillators, some methods yield precise configurational averages, potentially leading to faster convergence in optimization processes. Furthermore, the research found that the methods' precision is directly related to the order of the stochastic differential equation solver. In molecular dynamics simulations, resolving the motion of atoms within a molecule and the interaction with the surrounding environment typically involves solving large systems of stochastic differential equations. By leveraging the methods' precision evaluation, researchers can optimize the solver parameters to achieve the best outcome, ultimately speeding up the convergence of post-processing tasks such as quantum mechanical calculations.

Numerical relativity simulations allow us to study how binary black hole mergers interact with their surroundings. However, these simulations start only shortly before the merger and require predetermined initial conditions to proceed. Therefore, a significant task involves identifying the appropriate configuration for the binary system and its environment at this point in the process. In our research, we've been investigating the behavior of dark matter in the vicinity of black hole binaries of equal mass, discovering a consistent, long-lasting profile that emerges over several orbits. Conversely, systems with greater dark matter mass see overdensities scattered due to the binary's motion. Furthermore, regardless of initial configurations, systems typically converge to the established profile after a certain number of orbits; this convergence often results in the emergence of overdensities scattered across the background. Additionally, if matter is directly on the binary's orbit, it becomes captured as a result of a consistent, long-lasting flow of matter. All of these features were also observed in our simulations of binary black hole mergers surrounded by dark matter, with the exception of matter located near the point of merger, where a distinct configuration exists that is not represented by any of our binary systems.

We tackle the persistent issue of exponential stability for a stretched Euler-Bernoulli beam on a star-shaped graph with three equal branches. The outer points where these branches meet are fixed while rotating. The inner point is capable of moving in two ways, with rotational movement influenced by both elasticity and friction. A detailed analysis in a Hilbert space reveals how the spectrum's asymptotic distribution and structure evolve. It demonstrates that specific eigenvector characteristics form a complete and orthonormal basis. Consequently, we derive the exponential stability of the associated semigroup directly. Notably, we show that under these connectivity conditions, stability is guaranteed even in the absence of elasticity along the edges.

Researchers utilized acoustic lenses composed of PMMA to increase the detection area of sensitive devices and improve resolution but discovered these lenses introduced image distortion. This problem was investigated and a new lens material called Stycast 1090SI was proposed as an alternative. The acoustic properties of this novel material were examined alongside PMMA to determine its feasibility. Computational simulations and practical tests using two different materials, PMMA and Stycast 1090SI, showed both materials significantly enhance the detection capabilities of sensitive devices. Notably, the Stycast lens exhibited lower levels of distortion compared to the PMMA lens, which could have implications for photoacoustic tomography technology.

Our new method calculates a variation of eigenvector centrality for multi-layered networks that incorporate node importance across different layers. In these networks, defined by separate interconnected graphs without connections between different layers, the value of a node's centrality is determined by the sum of the values of the connected nodes within each specific layer, similar to traditional eigenvector centrality calculations. Unlike standard approaches, our approach takes into account the relationships between different network layers and their respective impact on the centrality values. Unlike current multi-layer eigenvector centrality frameworks that account for inter-layer connections, our approach uses a separate set of equations that can be solved using a hybrid algorithm.

We tackle the issue of non-blind deblurring and demosaicking on noisy raw images using a learning-based approach tailored to handle these images directly, with an innovative new component that simultaneously demosaicks and deblurs them in an accurate and efficient way. To train this model, we utilize real-world camera data transformed into raw images through a realistic process, mimicking real-world camera functions. By doing so, we demonstrate the advantages of our single-stage model over traditional approaches combining demosaicking and deblurring modules, according to objective performance metrics. Additionally, our method is capable of removing a camera's intrinsic blurring effect, which effectively acts as a range finder, resulting in a highly accurate deblurring.

Recently, we introduced the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra as a semi-direct sum of the anti-symmetric generators of the Lorentz algebra and the symmetric generators of the Poincar\'e algebra. In this letter, we generate the $R$-Poincar\'e algebra's characteristic equation to obtain the de Sitter spacetime configuration. The new algebra allows for a more direct derivation of the de Sitter's Ricci and Klein-Gordon equations.

This study introduces an open source Python framework that utilizes background knowledge and observational data for the purpose of inferring causal relationships. This framework is comprised of the 'cdt' package, which executes a comprehensive causal discovery process to identify the causal interactions and the causal network structure among the variables, drawing from established methodologies including those from 'Bnlearn' and 'Pcalg', in addition to pairwise algorithms like ANM. The framework is available on GitHub under the terms of the permissive MIT License.

This study investigates how spheres interact with water upon impact, specifically the process known as surface seal that occurs as the sphere enters the water's surface. This surface seal regime, found between low and high-speed impact velocities, features a distinctive "splash dome" formation. Empirical rules exist for predicting splash-related phenomena at both slow and high-speed impact rates; however, these rules fail to account for the complex "splash dome" behavior observed in the intermediate speed range. In an effort to fill this gap, we present a new theory that explains the formation of the "splash dome" through the lens of fluid conservation, specifically for spheres hitting water at intermediate speeds of up to 10 m/s. This theory produces a critical ratio of the splash dome's height to the sphere's radius that can be used to identify when the surface seal regime occurs during intermediate-speed sphere impacts.

A well-known hypothesis posits that gravity at a quantum level must be devoid of universal symmetries. We studied an array of Type IIB four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ effective field theories to uncover the range of universal symmetries potentially present and then investigated why they are avoided. Generalized $\theta$-terms emerge as crucial elements in these theories. These $\theta$-terms generate nonlinear connections between axion fields and quadratic gauge field strengths which can be used to break many universal symmetries. If we consider charged states as part of the scenario, additional universal symmetries may be destroyed, yet we found that the $\theta$-terms yield a Witten-like effect that indicates that the range of charged states is composed of an endlessly populated, universal one-body sector together with diverse, universally neutral multi-body states.

Mobile device owners frequently require running sensitive security applications alongside unverified, potentially malicious software, which necessitates reliance on device hardware and system software components working together to isolate sensitive data safely. 

This often involves costly and impractically complicated system redesigns to accommodate limited hardware components, which limits adoption. 

To overcome these challenges, we present a novel multi-domain hardware design for smartphones that allows secure partitioning of device resources. 

This design includes two integrated hardware modules, each capable of operating independently, which reduces the reliance on external hardware components to isolate data safely. 

We present a practical demonstration of this concept using Intel's Core i5 architecture and demonstrate our method's effectiveness by running multiple security applications on a single device. 

Our evaluations indicate that our approach has minimal performance impacts while providing enhanced security, which we believe holds promise for applications beyond smartphone security.

We investigated the challenges of robust reinforcement learning in scenarios where an adaptive adversary intentionally manipulates rewards and transition probabilities. The adversary's influence is confined to no more than an $\epsilon$ fraction of all training episodes. Notably, this attack model surpasses previously considered methods. We established a key finding that no reinforcement learning algorithm can discover an optimal policy better than $O(\epsilon)$ under these circumstances. Interestingly, we discovered that the natural policy gradient method can be robust when the corruption is bounded and is capable of finding an $O(\sqrt{\epsilon})$-optimal policy. We developed a Filtered Policy Gradient (FPG) algorithm, capable of tolerating unbounded reward corruption, and achieved an $O(\epsilon^{1/4})$-optimal policy. The FPG algorithm represents a pioneering solution to robust reinforcement learning in scenarios with significant adversarial interference. Moreover, we validated the effectiveness of the FPG algorithm through successful experiments on multiple benchmark environments.

We uncover an unselectable version of the box game paradox, featuring players making remarkably accurate predictions of unknown real numbers without access to relevant information. Additionally, our analysis confirms the requirement of choice in solving the classic problem and examines alternative configurations of the game.

Our calculations using first-principles methods reveal that cubanite exhibits unusual orbital selectivity, with electrons occupying certain molecular orbitals while being localized in other atomic ones. This phenomenon is exceptionally rare in 3d transition metal compounds, providing a theoretical basis for the experimentally observed lack of charge disproportionation, anomalous Mössbauer spectra, and ferromagnetic coupling between adjacent iron ions.

A burgeoning field in quantum physics, known as multi-phonon physics, is driving research and development of quantum systems that interact with phonons in a precise, controllable manner. To contribute to this effort, we are proposing a novel application for dark states within semiconductor quantum dots. These dark states, which typically do not interact with light, can be transformed into a viable resource through the use of strong exciton-phonon interactions. By leveraging this approach, we show that dark excitons, which suffer from loss due to spontaneous phonon emission but offer longer lifetimes than bright excitons, can be created in a cavity-based system under resonant conditions. Furthermore, we have demonstrated theoretically that our approach can generate dark-state exciton phonon modes with high coherence properties and distinct resonance frequencies corresponding to distinct phonon modes, both of which are essential characteristics of systems that interact with phonons in a precise manner. Ultimately, this could enable the development of quantum gates that rely on phonon interactions with dark states.

Our investigation focuses on a 2D electronic lattice from a non-symmorphic wallpaper group.  We're examining a herringbone lattice with two types of glide symmetries in perpendicular directions using a nearest-neighbor tight-binding model. This model reveals the dispersion relationships of your electrons, guaranteeing the presence of two isomorphic Dirac cones within this lattice. These cones can be modified through the application of a shear strain, resulting in the convergence of two Dirac points and the creation of a Dirac cone along a line of high symmetry within the Brillouin zone. This transformation is controllable using the coupling between two neighboring sublattices in the model. Additionally, this change can be adjusted with the strength of this coupling, either pushing the electrons up or down within the Dirac cone. This distinctive property may allow this kind of lattice to operate as a pressure sensor for materials that have Dirac cones at the K-points, like graphene and transition metal dichalcogenides.

Quantum states known as single-photon catalyzed coherent states (SPCCSs) can be generated via quantum-optical catalysis using beam splitters or parametric amplifiers. These states occur when a coherent state and a single-photon state interact in two input ports, and a photon is detected in a specific output channel. We examine the success probabilities associated with detecting these states, as they vary significantly depending on the catalytic device used. Notably, our analysis reveals that states produced by beam splitters and parametric amplifiers exhibit the same characteristics when analyzing the distribution of photons. We thoroughly investigate the unique quantum properties of SPCCSs, including sub-Poisson statistics, anti-bunching effects, and quadrature squeezing. These findings demonstrate that SPCCSs possess abundant non-classical behavior, thereby conferring a quantum advantage for executing various technological tasks.

In General Relativity using the Newman-Penrose formalism, the use of bivectors plays a key role in identifying the precise solutions to Einstein's field equations. This review focuses on explaining the fundamental principles and detailed calculations of bivectors within the Newman-Penrose formalism, specifically by converting a complex self-dual electromagnetic field from the standard Minkowski space basis to the complex null tetrad basis. As a result, we derive the complex coefficients of the Weyl tensor in the context of Newman-Penrose formalism.

A recent framework combining artificial neural networks and mixed integer linear programming for designing chemical compounds has been built upon to create a new method for polymer inference. This new method incorporates a unique way of depicting polymers using monomers, new descriptors that capture their structure, and employs linear regression in the predictive framework. Computational trials have demonstrated that the proposed approach excels in predicting specific chemical properties in polymers, also successfully modeling compounds composed of up to 50 non-hydrogen atoms within a monomeric structure.

This paper presents a unified approach to addressing certain complex optimization challenges. Problems of control, estimation, and system design can be redefined as optimization problems subject to specific constraints. However, given the infinite dimensionality of these issues, it becomes necessary to employ numerical techniques to approximate a solution. We explore specific methods used in simultaneous direct approaches, specifically the transcription process. Our focus is on collocation, residual integration, and Runge-Kutta schemes, highlighting their applications to a case study related to the ventilator shortage during the COVID-19 pandemic. Our study investigated the possibility of ventilating more than one patient on a single ventilator by optimizing the breathing parameters of the patients, with preliminary results showing promising outcomes.

Identifying tumors in the esophagus from CT scans can be very difficult for humans or computer systems due to low contrast, the varying shape of the esophagus, and the presence of external objects such as feeding tubes. To compensate for these difficulties, doctors often rely on supplementary information from other imaging techniques, medical histories, and endoscopic findings. Acquiring and combining these sources of information is time-consuming and sometimes produces inconclusive results. In this study, we investigate the potential for a more streamlined clinical approach that solely utilizes CT scans for automatically identifying and outlining tumors in the esophagus with satisfactory precision. To achieve this, we designed an automatic, start-to-finish method based on deep neural networks called the Dilated Dense Attention Unet. This model leverages spatial and channel attention mechanisms in dense blocks to prioritize specific features and regions. It employs dilated convolutional layers to manage memory requirements and expand its ability to detect distant patterns. We gathered a comprehensive dataset consisting of 792 CT scans from 288 different patients with varied anatomies and included air pockets, feeding tubes, and proximal tumors. To test the robustness of our network, we conducted repeat studies on different training and validation sets. Our model produced a dice similarity coefficient (DSC) of 0.79, a mean surface distance of 5.4 mm, and a Hausdorff distance of 14.7 mm for 287 test scans. These results demonstrate the efficacy of a simplified, CT-only

The expense associated with drilling offshore wells is significant and these sites frequently contain complex hydrocarbon reservoirs. Achieving optimal well placement and reducing costs necessitates real-time geosteering. This process is usually supported by up-to-date formation evaluations derived from the interpretation of well logs acquired during drilling. For this application, a system was devised to conduct a thorough evaluation of well logs, incorporating a module for constrained inverse problems to obtain resistivity and density estimates deep within the well bore. These estimates were enhanced by coupling with a sparker-based bio-temperature measurement system to account for temperature fluctuations affecting the well logs. The proposed approach was evaluated using synthetic and actual well log data, and the results showed a notable improvement in formation evaluation. Furthermore, this method was successfully tested on real wells, facilitating real-time geosteering.

Named entity recognition (NER) is a fundamental task in natural language processing and a core extraction technique, extensively used to retrieve text-based information for further analysis. One type of NER, nested NER, focuses on recognizing entities within other entities. Most existing nested NER studies apply linear models, which do not adequately capture the hierarchical nature of nested entities. This work overcomes this limitation by modeling nested entities as an integrated whole and proposing a new parsing algorithm to accurately identify all entities at once. Moreover, to address the lack of corpus-level information in NER, this study introduces features based on corpus statistics, including Point-wise Mutual Information, to enhance model performance and adaptability from sentence-level to corpus-level. Our experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art or near-state-of-the-art results on standard benchmarks and showcase significant improvement in domain adaptation through the proposed holistic modeling.

We extend the use of tropical methods to counting in arithmetic problems, such as enumerating objects in higher-dimensional spaces using values from specific algebraic structures, over fields that have been modified to have special values, such as plane quartics with specific tangent properties as a reference. We look at curves defined by equations that are smooth, or at least have smooth properties in certain situations, over such modified fields. We express obstacles to counting these curves and their associated tangencies by altering the structure of these curves and their starting properties, focusing on edges and how they connect. We show that by understanding how these curves and their starting properties change when modified, we can calculate the relative importance of these curves when counting them using these specific algebraic structures, or "GW-multiplicity". This allows us to verify a previously proposed mathematical relationship involving these curves and their counts. This verification relies on a deeper understanding of how the algebraic structures of these fields are related, especially when these fields are modified to have special values, or "residue fields".

Research into the location detection of mobile nodes within wireless sensor networks is currently ongoing. We develop and test an innovative RSSI-based location finding method suitable for 802.15.4 (ZigBee) networks. To counteract interference between different technologies operating in the same frequency range, we design and execute a new method for calculating the distance between nodes. The aim of this approach is to minimize the average error in location estimation, and when compared to ideal, interference-free results, we have achieved a level error of 4.75 meters using real-world hardware.

Multilingual individuals possess a high level of proficiency in two or more languages, enabling effective written and oral communication across multiple languages. When communicating, they may blend languages, also known as code-switching or code-mixing, by switching between different languages within a single utterance. This research explores current NLP developments, constraints, and potential obstacles in tackling five critical issues affecting multilingual communities: crisis management, healthcare, election campaigns, fake news dissemination, and hate speech. To move forward, we outline potential future datasets, models, and resources to enhance NLP applications for societal betterment, exemplified through an analysis of code-mixing between English and Hindi but with implications for other language combinations as well.

Human-generated descriptions are commonly used to train and evaluate image description systems, which are typically ranked based on their similarity to these descriptions. This method's reliability hinges on the quality of these descriptions. Since, as demonstrated in Section 2, current datasets are inadequate, I believe we require more precise guidelines balancing visually impaired users' needs and practical description generation feasibility. High-quality reference data could be ideal for system evaluation, yet we should also consider other alternatives.

Tantalum oxide compounds, with the formula Ta$_2$O$_5$, are distinguished by unique properties including high dielectric values and minimal reflectivity. Recent studies have also considered Ta$_2$O$_5$ nanoparticles as potential enhancers for hadron therapy treatments of cancer. To understand the material's electronic properties, researchers have used theoretical simulations from first principles. Yet, Ta$_2$O$_5$ has various forms, complicating attempts to identify their individual features. To resolve this issue, researchers used time-dependent density functional methods to study the energy loss function in Ta$_2$O$_5$, specifically in its optical state, and across different polymorphs. These studies have demonstrated that experimental reflection loss signals can be interpreted assuming that both the optical state and the d-band in Ta$_2$O$_5$ contribute to the reflection loss. Moreover, calculations have shown that both the optical state and the d-band in Ta$_2$O$_5$ contribute to the reflection loss, and that the d-band plays a key role in the energy loss of Ta$_2$O$_5$ when interacting with electrons in materials like water and organic compounds.

Previous studies attributed online misinformation dissemination to user irrationality, bias, and technology limitations. Conversely, a recent theory proposes linking misinformation spread to underlying societal factors, including those related to personality traits. To test this, we conducted an original survey where we linked state-level personality trait data to internet users' news circulation habits. The results show that certain personality traits are indeed associated with the spread of misinformation and new information, including claims verified as false. Additionally, we identified specific traits associated with the dissemination of misinformation, namely low conscientiousness in online communities, and low agreeableness when interacting with news, including misinformation. The data further reveal variations in misinformation dissemination at the state level, with no clear online-offline divide. The research also distinguishes between information and misinformation circulation, highlighting distinct underlying factors for each. The results provide insights into online information dynamics and the spread of misinformation and highlight the necessity of targeting specific personality traits in designed interventions aimed at curbing misinformation dissemination.

We introduce a groundbreaking, efficient, and user-friendly detection algorithm called HALFADO. HALFADO uses a limited number of human judgments to effectively identify anomalies in real-time, high-frequency data streams. Implementing a precise detection system is crucial for empowering human teams across the digital world by providing reliable decision support. As these systems have profound consequences for the trustworthiness of the internet, empowering human teams is vital for the reliability of the internet. Halfado addresses a key challenge in learning from inconsistent, real-world data and can also mitigate the negative impact of confirmation bias. We discuss the theoretical advantages of running halfado and other suitable algorithms that combine human and machine learning capabilities. Additionally, we present practical benefits of using halfado in real-world applications.

Humans employ spoken language to efficiently teach other people various skills. Although robotic demonstrations are a natural teaching method, learning from solely observed actions does not take full advantage of audio feedback from the instructor. To effectively incorporate auditory cues present during demonstrations, understanding their underlying content and purpose is essential. This study examines audio input from humans instructing a robot using Sawyer via spoken language by analyzing three key features: speech duration, tone variation, and speech content. Evaluating these features across four dimensions, it was discovered that instructors frequently use the same vocabulary to describe specific task elements despite varying situations such as task types, audio instructions, and errors encountered during demonstrations. However, differences in speech patterns including duration and inflection are present across these conditions, showing that human speech carries significant, potentially valuable information for enhancing robotic learning through demonstration-based methods.

Building on previous work, we propose an algorithm to randomly generate ordered trees of any degree, based on a pre-specified sequence of numbers representing possible node connections. Our method allows for the generation of binary, n-ary trees, or those with various connection patterns. We demonstrate that this algorithm is both accurate and efficient, running in O(n) time with 'n' representing the number of desired nodes. Additionally, we explore potential applications of the algorithm, illustrating its use in deriving formulas by utilizing the underlying proof of correctness.

Quantum field theory complexity is particularly hard to define, especially when transitioning beyond simple free models and their corresponding Gaussian representations. A promising approach to address this difficulty involves the study of conformal field theories in 1+1 dimensions, specifically focusing on the universal sector of the energy-momentum tensor in this context. A key unifying framework consists of Euler-Arnold equations and their broader integro-differential generalizations, ensuring the well-posedness of state or operator complexity optimization problems. Our comprehensive investigation extends upon our prior findings in arXiv:2005.02415, delving into intricate details of employed methodologies. A notable discussion involves differential regularization strategies, solving the integro-differential equation for Fubini-Study state complexity, and further exploring the underlying geometric properties.

Conversational interfaces are becoming ubiquitous, and systems with these interfaces are being widely used in various settings by many individuals. Although they have achieved considerable success, the infrastructure for automated testing of these systems lags behind traditional software systems. To enhance the quality of conversational systems, developers require a robust automated testing framework that streamlines the process of crafting, executing, and updating test cases. This paper outlines our ongoing research in developing an automated testing framework for conversational agents in Python, and highlights the key challenges faced in this endeavor. Specifically, we highlight the difficulties in establishing a precise specification for desired system behavior and comparing the meaning of utterances.

Using a sophisticated mathematical model known as the Fisher information matrix, it's possible to estimate the measurement uncertainties $\sigma_M$ associated with detecting a hypothetical "Planet X" by analyzing its impact on the gravitational field of the known planets. Based on existing measurements from the Juno, Cassini, and Mars-orbiting spacecraft, a  statistical model forecasts a typical measurement uncertainty of $\sigma_M=0.22M_\oplus (d_x/400\,\textrm{AU})^4.$  Under ideal conditions, a  Planet X with a mass five times that of the Earth at a distance of 400 AU can potentially be confirmed with certainty across the entire sky, whereas a  Planet X of the same size but located at 800 AU can be confirmed with the same level of certainty only over about 5% of the sky. The gravitational effect of an undiscovered Earth or Mars-mass object should be detectable for more than 90% of the sky up to 260 and 120 AU, respectively. Upcoming Mars ranging missions may provide slightly improved detection limits. The project also explores the effectiveness of highly accurate astrometry (determining positions and movements) of approximately 8000 Jovian Trojans from 2023 to 2035 using data from the upcoming Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST).  It's determined that optical Trojan astrometry faces several dominant systematic errors which could potentially be addressed internally with data from varying

Previous studies have demonstrated that Translation Memory (TM) can enhance Neural Machine Translation (NMT) performance. Unlike existing approaches which rely on bilingual corpora for TM and employ source-side similarity searches, our proposed framework leverages monolingual data and retrieves memories in a cross-lingual manner. Notably, our framework offers both TM-assisted NMT models and monolingual encoder updates as TM-related components can also be viewed as pre-training steps for NMT. Experimental results indicate that all our TM-related baselines outperform the NMT baseline, and our method incorporating the monolingual encoder update achieves the highest performance improvements of +2.73 BLEU on the parallel test set and +3.42 BLEU on the low-resource parallel test set.

Researchers have suggested that specific patterns in the Cosmic Microwave Background, namely low-variance circles and Hawking points, could provide evidence for the Conformal Cyclic Cosmology model. These patterns are predicted to originate from previous black hole mergers and evaporation events. We analyzed the Planck and WMAP data using a machine learning tool called HawkingNet, and initially found potential anomalies resembling low-variance circles and Hawking points. However, these anomalies were later removed, and upon re-examination, we found no statistically significant evidence supporting the existence of low-variance circles or Hawking points. Our analysis does indicate the presence of local non-Gaussian fluctuations in the CMB, suggesting that the real sky may differ from theoretical predictions.

This paper builds upon previous work of the second author with Daskalopoulos and Vazquez, which involved introducing a Yamabe flow based on fractional curvature and demonstrating the existence of mild solutions. The current research expands on that study by establishing the convergence of the flow under certain data conditions within a broader framework. The new results are derived from an approach simplified by Struwe in his book.

To recognize new categories from minimal labeled data, few-shot learning has been rapidly evolving in recent years. However, traditional methods that rely on average operations for calculating prototypes often struggle due to the influence of outliers. This research introduces a new, effective framework that utilizes an episodic prototype generator module to create more representative prototypes from limited support data, reducing the impact of outliers and resulting in preferable models. The framework's ability is further showcased by the substantial improvement it yields over baseline models and the comparable performance it achieves to existing methods on datasets like miniImageNet, tieredImageNet, and cross-domain benchmarks (miniImageNet to CUB-200-2011).

Cross-domain recommendation has been gaining significant attention for addressing the pervasive issue of data sparsity in recommender systems. Single-target and dual-target CDR approaches are often hindered by the limitations of requiring at least one well-supplied domain and over-reliance on domain-agnostic preferences, which is impractical given the ubiquitous sparsity in real-world scenarios. To address these shortcomings, we introduce a novel framework called Multi-Sparse-Domain Collaborative Recommendation (MSDCR) that tackles multi-target cross-domain recommendation in multiple sparse domains. In contrast to conventional CDR methods, MSDCR considers all participating domains as equally data-poor, thereby simultaneously enhancing the recommendation performance across each domain. We devise a Multi-Domain Separation Network (MDSN) and a Gated Aspect Preference Enhancement (GAPE) module to augment a user's specific aspect preferences in each domain by transferring complementary preferences from other domains, while maintaining domain-specific uniqueness through adversarial training and dynamically determining the degree of preference enhancement using GAPE. Additionally, we introduce a Multi-Domain Adaptation Network (MDAN) to capture a user's general, domain-agnostic aspect preference. By integrating the domain-specific aspect preference and the domain-agnostic aspect preference, MSDCR attains a thorough understanding of user preferences across each data-poor domain. The empirical evaluations on real-world datasets unequivocally demonstrate the superiority of our MSDCR model over state-of-the-art single-domain and CDR models.

Convex optimization issues often take on a more manageable form when represented with conic formulations that leverage a wide variety of exotic cones. Exotic cones in this context, refer to specialized geometric shapes with properties enabling efficient implementation of computational tools, specifically barrier oracles for their own and dual shapes. This paper introduces Hypatia, an interior-point solver designed to handle these complex shapes with ease. Developed using Julia and interfacing with JuMP, Hypatia can utilize a wide assortment of predefined exotic cones. It then generates simplified equivalent formulations for various optimization applications that can provide significant improvements in processing speed and memory consumption. The proposed method demonstrates a marked improvement in problem-solving efficiency when compared to more conventional and complex conic formulations.

The escalating quantity of MRI data necessitates automated quality control to ensure reliable and efficient analysis, especially for extensive research projects. Several institutions have developed in-house solutions, but these are typically confined to specific applications and have limited scalability due to heavy reliance on manually crafted features and learning algorithms. In contrast, our group has successfully pioneered a data-driven, broadly applicable QC framework across multiple analysis tasks, leveraging deep learning-based image analysis networks to extract pivotal features from MRI data. We refined and perfected this framework through extensive testing on large, publicly available datasets, notably the ADNI-GC-PDC's 3099 structural MRI scans. Our results demonstrate notable enhancements in both classification and regression metrics when comparing the performance of our automated QC system to that of leading research institutions. Notably, our approach has exhibited superior precision in identifying poor-quality scans, alongside remarkable accuracy in estimating measurement outcomes.

To understand how private electric vehicles influence the recovery of power grids following outages, we developed a mathematical framework that incorporates decentralized decision-making in both transportation and energy systems. We utilized multi-agent optimization to model this process and overcame computational challenges through an efficient algorithm based on precise reformation. Numerical analysis was conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, yielding valuable policy insights and paving the way for further study into grid resilience with private EVs within interconnected transportation and energy networks.

Intel's Optane DC Persistent Memory Module (DC PMM) has reached commercial viability as the first commercially available nonvolatile memory DIMM. It offers fast, byte-granular data access similar to DRAM, combined with power-fail safe storage. In-depth performance evaluations have shown Optane DC PMMs to provide outstanding results, outperforming traditional DRAM in specific scenarios while demonstrating comparable performance in benchmark-based testing. Furthermore, research has indicated that Optane DC PMMs can effectively utilize up to 256GB of persistent memory per socket, offering a substantial expansion on the 64GB per socket currently supported by DRAM technology. As a result of these capabilities, applications that require large memory footprints for data caching can significantly reduce their reliance on disk storage, achieving greater performance and efficiency as a consequence. In this article, we will explore strategies for optimizing application performance to take full advantage of Intel Optane DC PMMs. Specifically, we will examine two use cases one involving Java's Eclipse Mars and the other involving Linux's Redis in order to illustrate how persistent memory technology can enhance application performance.

The Motivation Dynamics framework, a concept explored in recent studies that applies bifurcations to model an autonomous agent's decision-making processes, is further developed to accommodate multiple autonomous entities in this paper. We demonstrate how the framework's capabilities can be expanded to capture persistent, cooperative behavior between agents meeting at specific locations, and through in-depth analysis and numerical data, reveal that this extension exhibits a complex pattern indicative of a strange attractor.

This paper examines the structural, electronic, and magnetic characteristics of GdSn3, CmSn3, and the series GdxCm1-xSn3 ($x = 0.25$, $0.5$, and $0.75$) using a full-potential linearized augmented plane wave method within the generalized gradient approximation+U. We studied the fundamental properties of bulk GdSn3, CmSn3, and GdxCm1-xSn3 materials crystallizing in the AuCu3 structure. Our results match previous experimental and theoretical data on the GdSn3 compound and indicate that CmSn3 and GdSn3 both adopt a type-A anti-ferromagnetic configuration and display metallic behavior. Notably, the magnetic moment diminishes with rising Cm content in the GdxCm1-xSn3 series, while all compounds possess similar electronic characteristics.

The paper reviews predictions made by an extension of the standard model called the bilepton model, which involves changing the fundamental symmetry group from $SU(2) \times U(1)$ to $SU(3)\times U(1)$, while assigning the three fermion families in a non-consecutive manner. For consistency, three fermion families are necessary as indicated by triangle anomaly cancellation and asymptotic freedom. In the bilepton model, novel physical phenomena are predicted to occur, including bileptons and three types of heavy quarks: ${\cal D}$, ${\cal S}$, and ${\cal T}$. Theoretical calculations suggest that Quantum Chromodynamics will result in heavy quarks bonding to each other or light quarks to form composite particles like baryons and mesons that might be detectable with a next-generation 100 TeV particle accelerator but are too heavy for the current LHC.

The concept of ordered generating sequences (OGS) extends a fundamental property of finite abelian groups to non-abelian groups, providing a distinct generalization. According to its definition, any element within a group can be expressed as a product of various generator powers, arranged in a specific order. For the symmetric group Sn, R. Shwartz established a significant link between the ordered generating sequences and the standard Coxeter presentation. Our study extends this connection to the finite classical Coxeter group Bn by standardizing the ordered generating sequences, which allows us to identify exchange laws for Bn. Moreover, we establish a connection with the standard Weyl group action, giving us a technical tool to investigate the representation theory of Bn.

Utilizing the Pantheon SN Ia dataset and Sloan Digital Sky Survey, we've developed a method to calculate weak lensing convergence by combining data on the positions and photometry of foreground galaxies. A correlation between this approach and the residual Hubble diagram values of Type Ia supernovae holds a $3.6\sigma$ significance and is consistent with dark matter effects due to galactic halos. Furthermore, we constrained galactic halo properties, including the mass-to-light ratio $\Gamma$ and the radial distribution of matter density within haloes $\rho(r)$. Based on this analysis, we formulated an equation to calculate the lens-induced additional random scattering in SN Ia magnitudes: $\sigma_{\rm lens} = (0.06 \pm 0.017) \cdot (d_{\rm C}(z)/ d_{\rm C}(1))^{3/2}$. As a result, the lens-induced apparent magnitude dispersion will approach the same magnitude as intrinsic SN Ia scatter at $z \approx 1.2$. Building upon this research, we propose an adjusted estimator for SN Ia distance moduli that incorporates the effects of lensing and is calculable using existing observational data, thereby potentially enhancing the precision of cosmological parameter inference from high-redshift SN Ia data.

These are lecture notes for a 6-hour mini-course on stochastic partial differential equations presented at the University of Oxford in April-May 2021. 

The main objective of these lecture notes is to provide an in-depth explanation of the variational method for monotone and coercive stochastic partial differential equations. 

The necessary background on Hilbert space-based functional analysis, operator theory, and stochastic analysis has been recapitulated within the lecture notes and further relevant references are included. 

The concluding chapter covers the pathwise approach.

The development of efficient and controllable quantum communication networks will depend heavily on reliable creation and manipulation of solid-state devices that interface photons with electronic spins effectively. In silicon material, T-type damage centers have shown significant potential for this interface, thanks to their unique optical properties in the O-band region and long-lived electronic and nuclear spin lifetimes. Although research on these defect centers has so far been conducted as part of bulk silicon studies, we report the consistent creation of T-type damage centers within the entrance windows of silicon devices using ion implantation. These defects were created near the surface, within a specifically controlled depth, and demonstrated strong optical interaction when combined with a microdisk resonator. Notably, our work offers a promising approach for standardizing the creation of high-quality photon-spin interfaces for quantum communication networks.

MRI technology utilizes radio waves to scan the human body and obtain precise, pain-free diagnostic images. These images enable radiologists to visually assess anatomy and physiological processes within the body, ultimately facilitating early disease diagnosis and treatment. Advanced imaging capabilities, combined with sophisticated processing techniques, enable detection of hard-to-spot tumors. This assignment delves into Automated Tumor Detection by optimizing multi-resolution Pyramidal Wavelet Neural Networks, which can find tumors even in complex MRI images by analyzing differences in tissue density. The model's effectiveness is verified using real MRI data from the Brain Tumor Segmentation (BTS) competition.

In this research, we explore the properties of a novel algebraic variant of the degenerate Bernoulli polynomial $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$, as well as its corresponding degenerate Bernoulli number. This investigation is grounded in an innovative algebraic framework for generating functions and symbolic evaluation functions, allowing us to derive $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$. Our findings demonstrate intriguing connections with circulant matrices and Galois fields, while showcasing the potential for $\tilde{\beta}_{k}(m,x)$ to be applied in computationally efficient contexts.

The high activity levels of M dwarfs present a significant challenge for discovering exoplanets, as their stellar activity masks the signals from these celestial bodies. This problem requires an effective method for filtering out the stellar activity from the data sets, especially when searching for habitable Earth-like planets. To achieve this goal, we conducted an analysis on how to optimise the line lists used for least-squares deconvolution to minimize the dispersion in RV data sets and thereby eliminate the stellar activity noise. Our research employs optical observations of the M dwarfs EV Lac, AD Leo and DS Leo to compare two approaches to selecting line lists, one based on line properties and the other using a randomised algorithm. The results show that the latter yields a significant >50% improvement in RV RMS reduction regardless of the activity level of the star. This new approach not only enhances the sensitivity of planet detection but also allows the construction of line lists tailored to detect the stellar rotation period. Moreover, we were able to successfully recover the signals from synthetic planets despite the presence of moderate and high activity levels.

This research paper proposes a novel approach to simplify the process of estimating link quality between nodes in Wireless Sensor Networks, which is a crucial function. To support this, we introduce a new algorithm called BQLE, enabling efficient and accurate link quality estimation between nodes. Theoretical and practical aspects of BQLE are discussed in detail, and the algorithm's performance is verified through both analytical and practical evaluations.

For our task that considers context, a suitable object detector is needed.
Different object detectors exploit scene context for recognition in varying ways.
In this study, we examine the relationship between context exploitation and object
detector design. Context exploitation is characterized by either using global
information to recognize local objects (G2L) or employing a combination of global
and local information for concurrent object recognition (G&L). We also introduce
a novel context exploitation category, known as unlimited context (U)  where
objects with no inherent connection can be recognized with the use of scene context.
We thoroughly evaluated the context exploitation capabilities of six popular object
detectors across three distinct evaluation contexts. Our experimental results
indicated the suitability of each object detector based on context exploitation
category. Furthermore, we discovered context exploitation is a design choice
dependent on object detectors rather than their performance. Moreover, our findings
indicated that deep neural network object detectors generally follow the G2L rule.
However, they can be designed to utilize unlimited context. We also found that
using context from the entire image is not always necessary. Instead, object
detectors can be designed to identify objects within specific global context
configurations rather than the entire scene. Our work lays the groundwork for
further research on the context exploitation capabilities of object detectors.

The main objective of this paper is to investigate multiple solution possibilities for a specific Kirchhoff type elliptic system of equations that are given by the system of equations where $m\left(\sum^k_{j=1}\|u_j\|^2\right)\Delta u_i=\frac{f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)}{|x|^\beta}+\varepsilon h_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)$ holds for $i=1,\ldots,k$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, where $x$ belongs to the domain $\Omega$ and $u_i$ have defined boundaries at infinity. Additionally, the functions $f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)$ satisfy specific growth conditions, and the parameter $\varepsilon$ is very small, represented by the variable $\varepsilon$ in the equation. When the potential function $f_i(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)$ is given by $x^a f(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)$ with $a\geq 0$ for all $i$ and for all $(x,u_1,\ldots,u_k)\in \Omega\times \mathbb{R}^k$, it is proven that the mentioned system of equations has at least $k$-solution by applying a local link ground state solution and a local minimizer of an associated energy functional for $\v

We examine the concentration behavior of functionals of random vectors whose entries reside in the discrete cube. These vectors must adhere to either the stochastic covering property (SCP) or the strong Rayleigh property (SRP). Our findings concerning SCP measures yield new subgaussian inequalities of a bounded-difference type, extending classic results by Talagrand, Bobkov-Gouezou, and others. Our results concerning SCP also include quantitative bounds in the finite-case scenario. For functions within the SRP class, we establish stronger inequalities of a Bernstein-type, encompassing a broader range of applications, including polynomial and matrix-valued functions. These theorems can provide useful estimates for the total variation or Kolmogorov norms of relevant functionals, ultimately facilitating the application of concentration inequality theorems, particularly those by Bousch-Talagrand, Milman-Pajor, and others.

Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic greater than two, and consider the ring of power series $R$ over the Witt vectors of $k$, expanded in variables $t_1, \dots, t_d$. The main aim of this study is to generalize classical Fontaine-Messing theory to a base ring of the form $R$. Notably, for a smooth, proper scheme $X$ over $R$, we establish the existence of a Fontaine-Messing theory, yielding a crystalline torsion topological cohomology functor $\Phi_{\mathrm{cris}}(X)$, well-defined for crystalline torsion $R$-cohomology in dimensions $2$ and higher.

This study explores the double longitudinal-spin asymmetry in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering where hadron pairs' transverse momentum is not considered. Specifically, we investigate the cause of the cosine azimuthal asymmetry in hadron production, accounting for the connection between the helicity distribution $g_1$ and the twist-3 dihadron fragmentation function. Using a spectator model, we calculate the interference term between $s$-wave and $p$-wave and estimate this asymmetry at various experiments, including COMPASS, JLab 12 GeV, and the future EIC. Our analysis suggests that the cosine azimuthal asymmetry in SIDIS can serve as a key test for the dihadron fragmentation function.

We've established recently, much like our work on Deformed Special Relativity, that Fock's coordinate transformation can be developed from a novel, deformed form of the Poisson brackets.  Utilizing this approach, we successfully obtained the associated momentum transformation, which preserves the four-dimensional relationship between momentum and space, p_{\mu} x^{\mu}.  With the deformed algebra in hand, we derive the first Casimir invariant in this paper.  Following first quantization, we utilize the Klein-Gordon equation to show that Fock's spacetime corresponds to the de Sitter universe, whose spacetime radius can be defined by the invariant length representing the de Sitter hypersurface.

Wilberd van der Kallen translated this 1951 thesis into English, originally written by T.A. Springer. Springer investigated the method of categorizing conjugacy classes within the symplectic group Sp_n(K), specifically focusing on fields K with a characteristic other than two. His work revealed that each conjugacy class can be distinguished using a combination of invariant characteristics. These characteristics initially mirror those found in the general linear group – namely, irreducible polynomials and systems of non-negative integers – but also incorporate additional properties, such as unique configurations of Hermitian forms and quadratic forms, each belonging to a specific equivalence class.

This paper presents a Wikipedia-based entity recommendation framework that utilizes an embedding approach, where the Wikipedia database is hierarchically divided into layered graphs to extract entity features and learn entity representations. By combining the extracted information with a lightweight ranking method, this framework effectively suggests related entities to users on Wikipedia. We evaluate our approach through both offline and real-world online tests, demonstrating that our embeddings and recommendations exhibit desirable quality and user engagement. Furthermore, this framework delivers entity recommendations in both English and non-English languages for the Yahoo! Knowledge Graph, where Wikipedia constitutes a fundamental subset.

A key obstacle in kidney transplants arises from the incompatibility between donors and patients, which has been exacerbated by the growing scarcity of kidney donors. Desensitization techniques were developed to overcome the immunological difficulties of incompatible transplants, but they also increase the risk of transplant-related complications such as rejection, cancer, and viral infections. A comprehensive study has been undertaken to thoroughly assess the outcomes of kidney transplants from incompatible donors using desensitization methods.
